A The speed of light is increasing.
B The star is moving towards Earth.
C The frequency of each spectral line has increased.
D The wavelength of each spectral line has increased.

(2)

A lower than the frequency emitted by the source.
B equal to the frequency emitted by the source.
C higher than the frequency emitted by the source.
D zero.

(2)

1.3

A The wavelength detected by the listener is longer than the wavelength emitted.
B The wavelength detected by the listener is shorter than the wavelength emitted.
C The frequency detected by the listener is higher than the frequency emitted.
D The speed of sound in air increases.

1.4
An ambulance with its siren sounding moves at a constant speed towards a stationary observer, passes the observer, and then moves away at the same constant speed.

Which ONE of the following graphs best represents the frequency detected by the observer as a function of time?

A A graph that is constant throughout.
B A graph that shows a sudden increase at the moment the ambulance passes the observer.
C A graph that shows a sudden decrease at the moment the ambulance passes the observer.
D A graph that shows a gradual increase followed by a gradual decrease.

(2)

A source emits sound of frequency fs. The source moves towards a stationary listener at speed vs. The speed of sound in air is v.

Which ONE of the following expressions correctly gives the frequency fL detected by the listener?

A fL = (v / (v + vs)) fs
B fL = (v / (v − vs)) fs
C fL = ((v + vs) / v) fs
D fL = ((v − vs) / v) fs

4.1
A bat emits ultrasound of frequency 50 kHz while flying towards a moth at 8 m·s⁻¹. The moth is stationary. The speed of sound in air is 340 m·s⁻¹.

4.1.1 Calculate the frequency of the sound detected by the moth.

4.1.2 The sound reflects off the moth and is detected by the bat. Calculate the frequency detected by the bat.

(6)
questions.answer:
4.1.1

fL = (v / (v − vs)) fs
fL = (340 / (340 − 8)) (50000)
fL = (340 / 332) (50000)
fL = 51204.82 Hz

(3)

4.1.2

Now the moth acts as a stationary source of frequency 51204.82 Hz, and the bat is a moving listener approaching at 8 m·s⁻¹.
fL = ((v + vL) / v) fs
fL = ((340 + 8) / 340) (51204.82)
fL = (348 / 340) (51204.82)
fL = 52409.64 Hz

(3)

(6)

5.2
Two cars, A and B, are moving towards each other. Car A moves at 20 m·s⁻¹ and car B moves at 15 m·s⁻¹. Car A sounds its horn at a frequency of 600 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m·s⁻¹.

5.2.1 Calculate the frequency detected by the driver of car B.

5.2.2 After the cars pass each other, car A continues at 20 m·s⁻¹ and car B continues at 15 m·s⁻¹ in opposite directions. Calculate the frequency detected by the driver of car B now.

(6)
questions.answer:
5.2.1

The listener (car B) is moving towards the source, and the source (car A) is moving towards the listener.
fL = ((v + vL) / (v − vs)) fs
fL = ((340 + 15) / (340 − 20)) (600)
fL = (355 / 320) (600)
fL = 665.63 Hz

(3)

5.2.2

Now the source and listener are moving away from each other.
fL = ((v − vL) / (v + vs)) fs
fL = ((340 − 15) / (340 + 20)) (600)
fL = (325 / 360) (600)
fL = 541.67 Hz

(3)

(6)

questions.question:
5.3
A source of sound moves in a circle of radius 2 m at a constant speed of 10 m·s⁻¹. A stationary observer is positioned at a large distance from the circle. The frequency of the sound emitted by the source is 800 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m·s⁻¹.

5.3.1 Calculate the maximum frequency detected by the observer.

5.3.2 Calculate the minimum frequency detected by the observer.

5.3.3 Calculate the frequency detected when the source is at the point where its velocity is perpendicular to the line joining it to the observer.

(8)
questions.answer:
5.3.1

Maximum frequency occurs when the source moves directly towards the observer.
fL = (v / (v − vs)) fs
fL = (340 / (340 − 10)) (800)
fL = (340 / 330) (800)
fL = 824.24 Hz

(3)

5.3.2

Minimum frequency occurs when the source moves directly away from the observer.
fL = (v / (v + vs)) fs
fL = (340 / (340 + 10)) (800)
fL = (340 / 350) (800)
fL = 777.14 Hz

(3)

5.3.3

When the velocity is perpendicular to the line joining the source and observer, the component of velocity along the line of sight is zero.
fL = fs = 800 Hz

(2)

(8)

5.4
An observer is standing on a platform. A train passes the platform without stopping. The train's whistle emits sound at a constant frequency of 550 Hz. The train moves at a constant speed of 25 m·s⁻¹. The speed of sound in air is 340 m·s⁻¹.

5.4.1 Calculate the frequency detected by the observer as the train approaches.

5.4.2 Calculate the frequency detected by the observer as the train moves away.

5.4.3 Sketch a graph of detected frequency versus time for the observer from the moment the train approaches until it moves far away. Indicate the values calculated in 5.4.1 and 5.4.2 on the graph.

(10)
questions.answer:
5.4.1

fL = (v / (v − vs)) fs
fL = (340 / (340 − 25)) (550)
fL = (340 / 315) (550)
fL = 593.65 Hz

(3)

5.4.2

fL = (v / (v + vs)) fs
fL = (340 / (340 + 25)) (550)
fL = (340 / 365) (550)
fL = 512.33 Hz

(3)

5.4.3

Graph criteria:
• The graph shows a constant frequency of 593.65 Hz before the train passes.
• At the moment the train passes, the frequency drops abruptly to 512.33 Hz.
• The graph shows a constant frequency of 512.33 Hz after the train passes.
• Correct labels and values on the y-axis.
